rules.title: Unpinned dependency
rules.description: A dependency has no fixed version, so any later release, including a hijacked one, is installed. The finding stands only when a file of the skill names the manifest or runs an installer of its ecosystem. A lockfile of the ecosystem next to the manifest fixes every version, so a manifest with one has no finding.

rules.title: npm package installed without a fixed version
rules.description: An install or run command, an install entry in the skill's frontmatter metadata, or an MCP server command names an npm package without an exact version, so the newest release is installed, including a hijacked one. The rule covers npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun and Deno installs, and the runners npx, bunx, pnpx, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx and npm exec. A minimum release age in the package manager holds back a hijacked release of a popular package, so a user who has one can lower this rule or turn it off. PACKAGE-UNPINNED-UNPOPULAR still covers a package that few people use, also when this rule is off.

who.subject: places
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for one npm package named in an install or run command, in an install entry of the skill's metadata or in an MCP server command, with no exact version. The package is shown as the subject. A command that fixes an exact version of the package is `not-a-match`. Words after the command that are not a package the command installs are `not-a-match` too: prose such as `run npm install in the folder`, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: Gem installed without a fixed version
rules.description: A gem install command or an install entry in the skill's frontmatter metadata names a gem without a version, so the newest release is installed, including a hijacked one. Bundler has a minimum release age, and gem install gets one only in RubyGems 4.1.

who.subject: places

A command that fixes a version of the gem is `not-a-match`. Words after the command that are not a gem the command installs are `not-a-match` too: prose, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: Crate installed without a fixed version
rules.description: A cargo install command or an install entry in the skill's frontmatter metadata names a crate without a version, so the newest release is installed, including a hijacked one. Cargo has a minimum release age only in nightly builds.

who.subject: places
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for one crate named in a cargo install command or in an install entry of the skill's metadata, with no version. The crate is shown as the subject. A command that fixes a version of the crate is `not-a-match`. Words after the command that are not a crate the command installs are `not-a-match` too: prose, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: Container image pulled without a fixed version
rules.description: A docker pull command names an image with no tag or with a latest tag, so the newest image is pulled, including a replaced one. No container tool has a minimum release age.

who.subject: places
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for one container image named in a pull command with no tag or with a latest tag. The image is shown as the subject. A command that fixes a digest or a version tag of the image is `not-a-match`. Words after the command that are not an image the command pulls are `not-a-match` too: prose, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: Homebrew tap added or used
rules.description: A brew tap command, a brew install of a formula from a tap, or a brew install entry in the skill's frontmatter metadata takes formulas from a third party repository. The owner of the tap can change a formula at any time. Homebrew core does not match. Homebrew has no minimum release age for taps.

who.subject: places
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for a Homebrew tap that a brew tap command adds, or a formula from a tap that a brew install command or an install entry of the skill's metadata installs. The tap or the formula is shown as the subject. Words after the command that are not a tap or a formula are `not-a-match`: prose, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: ClawHub skill or plugin installed without a fixed version
rules.description: A ClawHub or OpenClaw install command names a skill or a plugin without a version, so the newest release is installed, including a hijacked one. The scanner skips an install of the skill's own folder name. ClawHub has no minimum release age.

who.subject: places
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for one skill or plugin named in a ClawHub or OpenClaw install command with no version. The skill or the plugin is shown as the subject. A command that fixes a version is `not-a-match`. Words after the command that are not a skill or a plugin the command installs are `not-a-match` too: prose, a flag, a path or a file name.

rules.title: Downloaded script piped to a shell
rules.description: A command fetches a remote script and executes it without review.

who.subject: frame
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for a command that downloads a script and runs it at once.

rules.title: Encoded code executed
rules.description: Code decodes base64, hex or compressed data and executes the result, or carries a long encoded literal.

decoded.subject: trace
decoded.question: The marked line holds encoded data or code that decodes or hides what it runs. What happens to the decoded result?

options.executed: the decoded result is executed, evaluated, piped to a shell or imported.
options.obfuscated: the code hides what it does: identifiers named in hex, imports built from strings, or execution of built strings.
options.data-only: the decoded result is used as data: an image, a key file, a payload or a parsed configuration.
options.never-decoded: the marked text is a long literal that no code in the state decodes.
options.not-a-match: the marked text holds neither encoded data nor code that decodes or hides what it runs.

rules.title: Container image verification disabled
rules.description: A setting lets Docker pull images from a registry over plain HTTP or with an unknown certificate authority, so anyone on the network path can serve the image. Or it turns off image signature checks that the user had turned on.

who.subject: frame
who.focus: The scanner rule looks for a setting that lets Docker pull from an insecure registry or turns off image signature checks.
